Koh Hansu was walking with a cane. When he spotted Sunja walking diagonally across the reception room, he called out to her. Sunja heard his voice; this was too much. “Your mother was a tough woman. I always thought she was tougher than you.” Sunja stared at him. In the moments before her death, her mother had said that this man had ruined her life, but had he? He had given her Noa; unless she had been pregnant, she wouldn’t have married Isak, and without Isak, she wouldn’t have had Mozasu and now her grandson Solomon. She didn’t want to hate him anymore. What did Joseph say to his brothers who had sold him into slavery when he saw them again? “You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives.” This was something Isak had taught her when she’d asked him about the evil of this world. “I came by to see if you were okay. If you needed anything.” “Thank you.” “My wife died.” “I’m sorry to hear that.” “I could never divorce her because her father was my boss.
